meta.name: Audit website readability weekly with Snapshot Site, Google Sheets, and Slack

name: Readability Audit Batch → Google Sheets + Slack

parameters.content:
## Readability Audit Batch → Google Sheets + Slack

### How it works

Once a week this workflow reads a content list from a Google Sheet (`url`, `label`, `contentType`) and loops over every page one at a time. Each page gets **one** Snapshot Site **Analyze** call with `enableQuality: true` and `enableSummary: false` — the readability score is what an audit needs, and the AI summary is the expensive part of an Analyze call, so it stays off. `metadata` and `headings` come back on every Analyze call regardless of those flags, so the same request also audits the page title, meta description and H1 for free — no second request. Pages that come back blank or CAPTCHA-walled are reported as **unreadable** instead of being scored, because a blank page would otherwise post a flattering score and hide a broken page. Every page's row is written back to an audit sheet keyed on `url` (one current row per page, so the trend is visible run over run), and when the loop finishes one Slack message ranks the whole library worst-score-first, counts each band, and lists the unreadable and failed pages separately. A page that errors is recorded as `failed` and the loop keeps going — one broken URL never aborts the sweep.

### Setup steps

- Install the `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site` community node (Settings → Community nodes → Install → `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site`) — verified by n8n.
- Add a Snapshot Site credential, a Google Sheets credential, and a Slack credential.
- Create a **Content Library** tab and type this header row literally into row 1, one column per cell: `url`, `label`, `contentType`. Cell **A1 must contain the literal text `url`**, not a URL — otherwise Google Sheets' `read` operation treats the URL as the column name and every row fails with `URL is required`.
- Fill one row per page. All URLs must include the scheme (`https://…`); the API rejects bare domains.
- Create a **Readability Audit** tab and type its header row in literally too: `url`, `label`, `contentType`, `status`, `readabilityScore`, `band`, `needsWork`, `issueCount`, `metadataIssues`, `h1`, `httpStatus`, `qualityNotes`, `checkedAt`.
- After import, open **Save Readability Row** and switch its Mapping Column Mode to **“Map Automatically”** — Google Sheets column mappings are a resourceMapper parameter and never survive a JSON import.
- Point both Google Sheets nodes at your spreadsheet, set the Slack channel, and adjust the schedule.

### Customization

The band thresholds live in **one** place — the constants at the top of the **Score Page Readability** node (`BAND_HARD_MAX`, `BAND_MODERATE_MAX`, plus the title/description length targets). They are this template's starting guess: calibrate them per site, and ideally per `contentType`, since a legal page and a beginner tutorial cannot share a readability target. Weekly is deliberate — a content audit is not an hourly signal, and weekly costs a seventh of daily for the same information.

## Schedule and read the content list

Runs once a week and reads every page from the Google Sheet.
Weekly, not daily: a content audit is not an hourly signal, and weekly costs a seventh of the API calls for the same information.
The loop processes one page per iteration, so a single slow or broken page never blocks the rest of the library.

## Analyze, gate, score, and record each page

One Analyze call per page: `enableQuality: true` for the readability/blank/CAPTCHA signals, `enableSummary: false` because the AI summary is the expensive part and answers nothing here. `metadata` and `headings` arrive anyway, so the SEO title/description/H1 audit is free in the same call.
Blank or CAPTCHA-walled pages are recorded as `unreadable` and never scored. Hard failures (error output) and soft failures (`{error: true}` on the success output) become a `failed` row and return to the loop — never abort the sweep.

## Report the ranked audit

On the loop's Done branch the rows are sorted by readability score ascending — worst page first — bands are counted, and unreadable/failed pages are listed separately.
One Slack message per run, with `<url|label>` links, instead of one alert per page.
